230972365_dfd1f8d3.text: Because of differing developmental origins, certain amygdala nuclei exhibit a distinct neuronal composition (Sah et al., 2003)(Davis et al., 2000). The BLA has a more cortical-like profile, primarily containing excitatory neurons, whereas the CeA and MeA have a striatal-like composition of largely inhibitory neurons (Sah et al., 2003)(McDonald, 2003)(McDonald, 1982). Another discrete set of inhibitory nuclei, known as intercalated cell clusters, is located at the intersection of the BLA and CeA (Marowsky et al., 2005).
